title: Homemade Smash Burgers
description: Crisp-edged smash burgers with melted American cheese, quick pickled onions and a punchy burger sauce in a toasted brioche bun.
intro: Smash burgers are the best argument for doing less. No breadcrumbs, no egg, no fuss: just well-seasoned beef pressed hard onto a screaming hot pan until the edges go lacy and crisp.
Make the sauce and onions first, toast the buns, and cook the patties in the last five minutes. They wait for nobody.

items.note: finely chopped, plus a splash of brine

method.title: Pickle
method.text: Toss the onion with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Leave for at least 15 minutes, stirring once.

method.title: Sauce
method.text: Mix all the sauce ingredients together and season. Chill until needed.

method.title: Portion
method.text: Divide the mince into 8 loose balls of about 75g. Don't season or pack them yet. Keep them cold.

method.title: Toast the buns
method.text: Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast in a large, heavy frying pan or on a griddle until golden. Set aside.

method.title: Smash
method.text: Get the pan as hot as it will go. Add 2–4 balls, spaced well apart, and immediately press each one flat with a sturdy spatula until about 1cm thick. Season the tops with salt and pepper.

method.title: Flip and melt
method.text: Cook for 2 minutes without moving until a deep brown crust forms at the edges. Scrape under each patty, flip, add a slice of cheese and cook for 1 minute more. Stack two patties per burger.

method.title: Build
method.text: Spread sauce on both halves of each bun. Add lettuce, the double patty and a tangle of pickled onions. Eat immediately.

tips: A sheet of baking paper between the meat and the spatula stops it sticking as you smash.
Only press once, in the first 30 seconds. Pressing later squeezes out the juices.

substitutions.note: Mature Cheddar or Monterey Jack, sliced thin so it melts quickly.
Potato rolls give a softer, classic diner bite.
A mix of beef and pork mince is excellent; keep the fat content around 20%.
